insights.summary: FY26 revenue rose 17% to ₹443 Cr with EBITDA of ₹100 Cr (22.6%) and PAT of ₹55.5 Cr; Q4 grew 38% with a 23.9% EBITDA margin. The new liquid-cooling skid business for data centres sold 617 skids worth ₹21 Cr in four months, and capacity goes from 6,000 to 15,000 skids a year in the next two quarters. Management guided about 35% revenue growth and a ~23% EBITDA margin for FY27, with skids at 20-22% of sales and the base business growing 15-20%.

what_changed.text: About 35% revenue growth for FY27, base business 15-20%
FY27 EBITDA margin about 23%, 25% in a couple of years
Skid capacity 2,000 → 6,000 → 15,000 a year; skids 20-22% of FY27 revenue
Capital for miniature bellows moved to liquid cooling

tone.label: confident
tone.quote: I'm happy to report that FY26 has been a great year for the company

analyst_questions.answer: Design work (now done in-house) and strict end-customer audits slowed dispatches against the ₹42 Cr mentioned last quarter.
Skids go to one US-headquartered cooling company's India arm under an exclusive deal; largest export customer is 25-26% of sales.
Relates to an interest waiver from AY 2018-19 that was reopened; management expects to win on appeal.
Average ₹3-3.25 lakh a skid; varies with data-centre design.

red_flags.text: All skid revenue comes through one customer under an exclusive contract; no order book disclosed.
₹40 Cr income-tax demand, roughly a year's profit, under appeal.
Skid dispatches lagged supply because of design and quality-audit bottlenecks.
Metal bellows ran below 20% utilisation in FY26 after US tariffs hurt the plan.

watch_next: Quarterly revenue growth near 35% and EBITDA margin near 23%
Skid revenue share and the 15,000 capacity going live
Outcome of the ₹40 Cr tax appeal
